transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I just can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, little lists I started and didn’t finish. I sit there trying to figure out what to do first, and then… somehow the whole day is gone.
Do you find it hard to focus on one task for a long time?

Yes… especially if it’s paperwork or something I have to really think through. Forms, insurance papers, even putting together a schedule for a program… I’ll keep finding some little thing to do first. It’s like my head feels tired before I even begin.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently?
I’m not sure. I mean… little things, maybe, but I don’t know if it’s more than anyone else my age. I haven’t really kept track.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I don’t think so… not really. I’m more the type to sit and think too long, if anything. I haven’t noticed myself doing things suddenly without thinking.
Do you have trouble organizing your daily activities?

Yes… that’s actually a big part of why I came in. I can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is covered with appointment papers for my husband, church flyers, senior center notes, lists I started and didn’t finish… and I just sit there, not knowing what to do first. Then the day’s gone.
Have you been feeling overwhelmed or anxious about your daily tasks and responsibilities?

Yes… I do feel overwhelmed. It’s mostly trying to get the day in order. I’ll sit at the kitchen table with all these papers—my husband’s appointments, church things, senior center notes, lists I started—and I just don’t know which one to do first. Then somehow the whole day is gone.
Do you have trouble remembering things that other people tell you?

Yes… I do. I’ll think I heard it, but then it just doesn’t stay. I’ve missed returning calls, left bills under other mail, forgotten errands I told my daughter I’d do… and I’ve realized too late I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments.
Have you noticed any difficulty with learning new information?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that specifically… I mean, I’m not taking classes or anything. Sometimes new instructions don’t stick right away, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Are you having difficulty managing your daily life because of these problems with organization and memory?

Yes… it’s gotten in the way. I had to step back from leading a big event at the senior center because I just couldn’t keep it all straight. And my daughter… she’s been checking behind me on bills and appointments now. I don’t like that, but I suppose she doesn’t trust me to manage it all by myself anymore.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yes… I suppose I do. Even when I’m trying to sit still, like in a meeting, I’ll catch myself rubbing my hands or tapping my foot. Sometimes I click a pen or shift around, and then I notice people looking over.
Do you find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Yes… pretty easily. If the television is on in the next room, or people start talking near me at the senior center, my mind just sort of goes there. Then I lose my place in whatever I was writing or trying to plan.
Have you noticed any significant decline in your ability to think and understand things compared to a few years ago?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a big decline in understanding things. It’s more that I get mixed up or lose track, but thinking itself… I’m not sure.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to make decisions or solve problems over the past few years?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a major change, I don’t think… decisions can feel harder sometimes, but I can’t say it’s been a big shift over the years.
Do you think your memory and thinking abilities have gotten worse over the past few years?
I’m not sure I’d say they’ve gotten worse, exactly. I notice little things, but… I can’t really tell if it’s a real change or just me having off days.
Do you think there's been a noticeable decline in your cognitive abilities, such as memory or thinking, over the past few years?
I don’t really know. I can’t say I’ve noticed a clear decline… it’s hard for me to tell.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your memory or thinking over the past few years that have affected your daily life?
I don’t think so… not in a way that’s really changed my daily life. I mean, I have moments, but I can’t say I’ve noticed something significant.
Do you think your difficulties with memory and thinking are worse now than they were 5 years ago?
I don’t really know. Five years is a long time to compare… I can’t say I’ve clearly noticed it being worse.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your language abilities, such as finding the right words or following conversations?
Not really… I mean, sometimes I pause for a word, but I don’t think it’s anything significant. I haven’t noticed a big change with conversations.
Do you think your difficulties with memory and thinking have interfered with your social relationships or work?

Yes… I suppose it has, some. I had to stop leading this big event at the senior center because I just couldn’t keep all the pieces straight anymore. And my daughter… she’s been checking my bills and appointments now, just to make sure I haven’t missed anything. She doesn’t really trust me to manage it all by myself like I used to.
Do you think your memory and thinking abilities have gotten worse over time?
I’m not really sure. I don’t have a clear sense of it getting worse over time… it’s just hard to compare.
